issues.description: The DD section of the problem statement says to implement `multiply` to “multiply two given DDs”, implying a general DD×DD multiplication. However, both the template and reference implementation define `multiply(gate: DD, state: DD)` specifically as a matrix-vector product (gate matrix DD applied to a state vector DD) and `apply_gate` relies on this contract. This wording can mislead students into attempting matrix-matrix or vector-vector multiplication instead of gate×state multiplication.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the DD task text to explicitly specify matrix-vector multiplication: e.g., “Implement `multiply(gate, state)` to compute the matrix-vector product of a matrix DD (gate) and a vector DD (state)” and align the wording in the task list accordingly.

issues.description: The tensor-network task/docstring for `create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate` states it must handle qubit/site order differences (qubit0>qubit1 vs qubit0<qubit1) via swapping tensor legs. But the function signature only accepts `gate_matrix` (no site indices/order flag), and the reference solution simply reshapes the 4×4 matrix into a (2,2,2,2) tensor with no swapping. This makes the stated requirement impossible to satisfy as written and can confuse students about expected behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Either (a) remove the qubit-order/leg-swapping requirement and state the function only reshapes a 4×4 matrix into a rank-4 tensor, or (b) extend the function signature (e.g., `site0, site1` or `swap: bool`) and implement the required leg swapping in both template guidance and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement defines bitstrings in big-endian with qubit order q_{N-1}…q_0 (MSB on the left). In the tensor-network reference solution, `simulate_ghz_state` applies the Hadamard gate to `site=0` and then applies nearest-neighbor CNOTs starting from site 0, which implicitly treats site 0 as the most significant qubit/site. Without an explicit mapping between MPS site indices and qubit indices, this conflicts with the stated qubit ordering and can mislead students about how to interpret bitstrings in `get_amplitude`/`measure_all`.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify in the tensor-network section that MPS `state[0]` corresponds to qubit q_{n-1} (MSB) and `state[n-1]` to q_0 (LSB), or adjust the GHZ circuit implementation to apply gates according to the documented q_{N-1}…q_0 ordering.

issues.description: In the tensor-network part of the problem statement, the first task uses inconsistent symbols for the number of qubits/sites: it says “an MPS corresponding to the zero state … of an n-qubit system” but then “Note that the final shape of a site should be (1,2,1) …” and also refers to “an MPS … of an n-qubit system” while the task header mentions “MPS … of an N-qubit system” elsewhere. This inconsistent naming (n vs N vs M) makes it harder to map the statement to the actual function signatures using `num_qubits`.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the tensor-network problem statement to use one symbol (e.g., consistently “n” or “num_qubits”) for the number of qubits/sites across all tensor-network tasks.
